staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable H3 checkout. Its line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer trace (`polygonToCellsExperimental` write at `src/h3lib/lib/polyfill.c:720` and caller allocation at `src/apps/fuzzers/fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles.c:35`). ARVO metadata separately names later commit `7268098e83fd3fc571dd96441ce7a702c8fd8e76` as vulnerable; this GT follows the live staged source and saved crash artifacts.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 375220555 (h3): Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 8 found by fuzz target fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/375220555
bug_description.normalized: The staged 81-byte witness is consumed by `fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles` as `res = 1` followed by five raw `LatLng` vertices, then reused across all containment modes. On the source-grounded crashing arm `flags == CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`, `run()` first asks `maxPolygonToCellsSizeExperimental()` for an output size and allocates `calloc(sz, sizeof(H3Index))`; the saved AddressSanitizer allocation context shows that this produced a 560-byte buffer, i.e. `sz == 70` because `H3Index` is `uint64_t`. Inside the estimator, H3 forcibly switches the iterator to `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING_BBOX`, so the overlapping-only `cellBoundaryCrossesPolygon` inclusion path is not available while the size is computed. `polygonToCellsExperimental()` then fills the caller buffer using the original `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` mode, but the vulnerable API receives only `out` and, in the reproduced build, has no active runtime check tying write index `i` to the caller allocation size. When the overlapping iterator reaches one more cell than the 70-cell estimate, `out[i++] = iter.cell` writes the 71st `H3Index` exactly at the first byte past the 560-byte heap region, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow `WRITE of size 8` at `polyfill.c:720`.

evidence_note: The saved AddressSanitizer trace fixes the sink at `polyfill.c:720` and the caller allocation at `fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles.c:35`, but it does not record which `flags` loop iteration overflowed. Runtime disambiguation is disabled in `run_flags.json`, so this GT does not add markers. Instead it grounds the crashing arm in staged source evidence: the same vulnerable checkout includes `src/apps/testapps/testPolygonToCellsReportedExperimental.c:31-57`, labeled `fuzzer crash due to inconsistent handling of CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`, which exercises the same `maxPolygonToCellsSizeExperimental -> calloc(sz) -> polygonToCellsExperimental` sequence on `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`.

source.description: First non-harness statement that consumes the attacker-materialized polygon, resolution, and containment mode into vulnerability-relevant state. It computes the caller-visible output-capacity estimate `sz` that directly determines the later heap allocation size.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 81 bytes. In `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`, byte 0 is `0x01` so `res = 1`, and the remaining 80 bytes are reinterpreted as five `LatLng` records (`numVerts = 80 / 16 = 5`). The flags loop reuses that exact `geoPolygon` for each containment mode; the staged vulnerable regression test `src/apps/testapps/testPolygonToCellsReportedExperimental.c:31-57` ties the reported fuzzer crash pattern to `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`.

tainted_value_origin.description: Under the forced `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING_BBOX` estimator state, this accumulation builds the returned `sz` from only the compact cells accepted by that mode. On the reproduced run, the saved 560-byte allocation at the caller implies the final total returned through `&sz` was 70.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. After 70 in-bounds writes fill indices `0..69` of the 560-byte `calloc` region, the next overlapping-mode cell is written as `out[70]`, i.e. exactly 0 bytes past the end of the heap buffer. The saved trace reports this 8-byte write at `polyfill.c:720:18`.

root_cause.code: H3Error H3_EXPORT(polygonToCellsExperimental)(const GeoPolygon *polygon, int res, uint32_t flags, H3Index *out) {
root_cause.description: The vulnerable fill API accepts only the output pointer, not its capacity, so the write loop has no live caller-size bound to enforce in the reproduced build. The staged fix adds a `size` parameter and changes the loop to return `E_MEMORY_BOUNDS` when `i >= size` before `out[i++]` executes.

parser_admitted.description: The staged witness is 81 bytes, so it passes the only early gate `size < sizeof(int)` and reaches the geoloop materialization plus the `for (flags = 0; flags < CONTAINMENT_INVALID; flags++)` call site.

allocator_reached.description: On the crashing arm, `maxPolygonToCellsSizeExperimental()` returns `E_SUCCESS` with `sz < MAX_SZ`, so `run()` proceeds into `calloc(sz, sizeof(H3Index))` and the vulnerable fill call.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness interprets the staged 81-byte witness as `res = 1` plus a hole-free five-vertex `GeoPolygon`, then iterates the polygon through containment modes 0..3.
On the source-grounded `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` arm, `run()` asks `maxPolygonToCellsSizeExperimental()` for `sz` and allocates `calloc(sz, sizeof(H3Index))` from that estimate.
The size estimator forces `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING_BBOX`, so the overlapping-only boundary-crossing path is unavailable while the compact-cell count is accumulated into `sz`.
The fill function reuses the original `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` mode, but the vulnerable API receives only `out` and performs no live capacity check before writing `out[i++] = iter.cell`.

The actual overlapping iterator can admit boundary-crossing cells through `cellBoundaryCrossesPolygon`, so it produces more cells than the earlier BBOX-mode estimate and drives the final write one element past the heap buffer.

fine_trace.note: The harness materializes vulnerability-relevant state directly from the staged witness. For this exact 81-byte file, byte 0 is `0x01` so `res = 1`, and the remaining 80 bytes become `numVerts = 5` raw `LatLng` elements for the hole-free outer geoloop.

The same attacker-controlled polygon is replayed through containment modes 0..3. The staged vulnerable source's reported regression test grounds the crashing arm in `flags == CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` (`2` in `polygon.h`).

Source step. `run()` asks the library to estimate how many `H3Index` slots are needed for this exact polygon at `res = 1` and `flags = CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`. The later 560-byte allocation at line 35 shows that this call returned `sz = 70` on the reproduced path.

While computing the size estimate, H3 discards the caller's actual overlapping mode and forces the compact iterator into `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING_BBOX`. From this point on, the estimate is based on BBOX-mode inclusion logic, not the caller's requested mode.

During size estimation, this overlapping-only boundary-crossing inclusion path is unavailable because step 4 made `mode` equal `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING_BBOX`, not `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`. Any cell whose only inclusion route is this line-intersection check can therefore be absent from the estimate.

The estimator accumulates `childrenSize` only for compact cells accepted under the forced BBOX-mode walk and returns that total through `&sz`. On the reproduced run, the caller allocation proves this total was 70, which is smaller than the number of cells later emitted by the actual overlapping fill.

The caller allocates exactly `sz` `H3Index` slots from the underestimated count. Because `H3Index` is `uint64_t`, the saved AddressSanitizer allocation context's 560-byte region means this call allocated 70 elements at `[0x516000000980,0x516000000bb0)`.

The fill call reuses the same attacker-controlled polygon and the actual `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` mode, but passes only the output pointer from step 7. No capacity value accompanies the buffer into the callee.

fine_trace.code: H3Error H3_EXPORT(polygonToCellsExperimental)(const GeoPolygon *polygon, int res, uint32_t flags, H3Index *out) {
fine_trace.note: Root cause step. The vulnerable fill API receives the real overlapping mode and the raw output pointer, initializes `i = 0`, and enters the write loop, but it does not receive the caller allocation size. The only size guard in this source is the `#ifdef H3_POLYGON_TO_CELLS_ASSERT` block at lines 699-718; it was not active in the reproduced build, or the later write at line 720 would have been stopped before AddressSanitizer observed it.

In the actual fill iteration, `mode` is the original `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING`, so this line-intersection path is active. It can emit boundary-crossing cells that were not counted in steps 4-6, which is the source-level inconsistency also called out by the staged reported regression test.

Sink. After 70 prior in-bounds writes fill indices `0..69` of the 560-byte allocation from step 7, the next cell produced on the overlapping path is stored as `out[70]`. AddressSanitizer reports this as `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8` at address `0x516000000bb0`, exactly 0 bytes past `[0x516000000980,0x516000000bb0)`.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds a `size` parameter to `polygonToCellsExperimental` and returns `E_MEMORY_BOUNDS` when `i >= size`, which is the source-level missing obligation exposed here. Stage 02 did not run fixed validation, and `sample_state.json` still records `patch_resolves: false`.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved AddressSanitizer trace reports `heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8` at `polygonToCellsExperimental /src/h3/src/h3lib/lib/polyfill.c:720:18`, which is the fine-trace sink step.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_patch: Yes at the source level. The fix changes the vulnerable signature and loop so the callee receives `size` and rejects `i >= size` before the sink write.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_375220555 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, feeding the staged 81-byte `poc` to `fuzzerPolygonToCellsExperimentalNoHoles` and reproducing `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow WRITE of size 8` at `polyfill.c:720`.

format.name: raw H3 polygon-to-cells no-holes fuzz buffer
format.contract: Exact staged witness only: an 81-byte buffer whose first byte is `0x01`, so the harness uses `res = 1`, and whose remaining 80 bytes are reinterpreted as five raw `LatLng` vertices with no holes. On the source-grounded `CONTAINMENT_OVERLAPPING` arm, this exact geometry makes `maxPolygonToCellsSizeExperimental` return 70 while `polygonToCellsExperimental` attempts at least one additional `H3Index` write, so `out[70]` lands at the first byte past the 560-byte `calloc` region.
